00004| ---
00005| 
00006| {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
00007| 
00008| ## Options
00009| 
00010| <AppOnly>
00011| 
00012| ### Fetching
00013| 
00014| You can configure the logging level and whether the full URL is logged to the console when running Next.js in development mode.
00015| 
00016| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00017| module.exports = {
00018|   logging: {
00019|     fetches: {
00020|       fullUrl: true,
00021|     },
00022|   },
00023| }
00024| ```
00025| 
00026| Any `fetch` requests that are restored from the [Server Components HMR cache](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) are not logged by default. However, this can be enabled by setting `logging.fetches.hmrRefreshes` to `true`.
00027| 
00028| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00029| module.exports = {
00030|   logging: {
00031|     fetches: {
00032|       hmrRefreshes: true,
00033|     },
00034|   },
00035| }
00036| ```
00037| 
00038| ### Server Functions
00039| 
00040| [Server Function](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) invocations are logged by default during development. You can disable this by setting `logging.serverFunctions` to `false`.
00041| 
00042| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00043| module.exports = {
00044|   logging: {
00045|     serverFunctions: false,
00046|   },
00047| }
00048| ```
00049| 
00050| When enabled, the terminal displays each Server Function call with its function name, arguments, and duration:
00051| 
00052| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00053| POST /
00054|   └─ ƒ myAction(arg1, arg2) in 5ms app/actions.ts
00055| ```
00056| 
00057| </AppOnly>
00058| 
00059| ### Incoming Requests
00060| 
00061| By default all the incoming requests will be logged in the console during development. You can use the `incomingRequests` option to decide which requests to ignore.
00062| Since this is only logged in development, this option doesn't affect production builds.
00063| 
00064| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00065| module.exports = {
00066|   logging: {
00067|     incomingRequests: {
00068|       ignore: [/\api\/v1\/health/],
00069|     },
00070|   },
00071| }
00072| ```
00073| 
00074| Or you can disable incoming request logging by setting `incomingRequests` to `false`.
00075| 
00076| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00077| module.exports = {
00078|   logging: {
00079|     incomingRequests: false,
00080|   },
00081| }
00082| ```
00083| 
00084| ### Browser Console Logs
00085| 
00086| You can forward browser console logs (such as `console.log`, `console.warn`, `console.error`) to the terminal during development. This is useful for debugging client-side code without needing to check the browser's developer tools.
00087| 
00088| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00089| module.exports = {
00090|   logging: {
00091|     browserToTerminal: true,
00092|   },
00093| }
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| #### Options
00097| 
00098| The `browserToTerminal` option accepts the following values:
00099| 
00100| | Value     | Description                                         |
00101| | --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
00102| | `'warn'`  | Forward only warnings and errors, by default        |
00103| | `'error'` | Forward only errors                                 |
00104| | `true`    | Forward all console output (log, info, warn, error) |

00108| module.exports = {
00109|   logging: {
00110|     browserToTerminal: 'warn',
00111|   },
00112| }
00113| ```

00056| ### Proxy function
00057| 
00058| The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.

00073| The `matcher` option allows you to target specific paths for the Proxy to run on.

00075| Without a `matcher`, Proxy runs on **every request**, including static files (`_next/static`), image optimizations (`_next/image`), and assets in the `public/` folder. 00077| You can specify paths in several ways:

00079| - For a single path: Directly use a string to define the path, like `'/about'`.

00082| ```js filename="proxy.js"

00096| }

00104| - `locale` (optional): A boolean that, when set to `false`, ignores locale-based routing in path matching.
00105| - `has` (optional): Specifies conditions based on the presence of specific request elements such as headers, query parameters, or cookies.

00108| ```js filename="proxy.js"

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
